entries.note: Whether it is 'not obvious' he is wrong is a hedged, subjective view of the evidence, and 'dud' has no shared measure. The underlying bet from August 12 belongs to a separate post.

entries.test: Whether the Axios/S&P Global survey data from August 2023 and similar surveys showed many companies struggling to deploy generative AI, citing cost and confusion.
entries.note: The deployment-struggle part is Axios's reporting, which Marcus relies on and endorses. 'No deployment, no revenue' is his own inference.

entries.test: Whether any documented enterprise-scale generative AI project has since been abandoned or judged a failure.
entries.note: This is a near-trivial forecast: one documented failure settles it.

entries.test: Whether prominent mainstream critical commentary on ChatGPT and generative AI (e.g., Gioia, the FT's Thornhill) had appeared by August 2023.
entries.note: 'Backlash' is vague. The plain reading is that prominent public criticism had emerged.

entries.test: Whether contemporary reporting documented Google's latest LLM producing offensive outputs, such as listing Hitler among 'greatest' leaders, in August 2023.
entries.note: Faithfulness relies on the post's Google example to make the vague 'problems' specific.
'Could be devastating' states a possibility. The hedged premise, that removing content requires full retraining, could be checked separately.

entries.test: Whether by August 2023 'sounds like ChatGPT' was used publicly as an insult (e.g., Christie's debate line about Ramaswamy), and whether ChatGPT had earlier been widely likened to AGI.
entries.note: This is hyperbolic. Only the core claim, that ChatGPT had become an insulting shorthand, can be graded.

entries.test: Whether reporting from mid-2023 showed rising financial pressures on OpenAI/ChatGPT, such as losses, compute costs, litigation exposure, or slowing usage.
entries.note: The claim is vague. Readers may weigh rising losses against fast-growing revenue differently.
This is an exclamatory summary hedged by 'it ain't over yet'. It commits to no measurable reversal.
